episode_title: EP. 90 - Inside the $10M Oil & Gas Fund: how to Limit Risk and Maximize Returns ft. Courtney Moeller

real_qa.q: What is the target internal rate of return and multiple for the OG6 Limited Partnership fund?
real_qa.r: The goal is to raise approximately $10 million to diversify amongst 40 different wells with an approximate IRR of 27% and a 2.1x return. Returns are modeled at $72 a barrel of oil, with each well producing 650,000 barrels of oil and 8 million cubic feet of natural gas on average.

real_qa.q: What is the tax deduction percentage available to investors in Iron Horse Energy Fund 1?
real_qa.r: Investors in Iron Horse Energy Fund 1 received approximately a 95.6% deduction, meaning every $100,000 invested yielded a $95,000 deduction that could be claimed against tax filings. This was achieved through intangible drilling costs, tangible drilling costs, and the depletion allowance.
real_qa.requete: Iron Horse Energy Fund 1 tax deduction

real_qa.q: How many wells have the partners invested in and what is their historical failure rate?
real_qa.r: The partners have invested into more than 1,200 wells over the last 18-19 years, out of which less than 1% have failed to produce commercially, with approximately 10 wells that did not produce at all. These wells are across 200 plus deals and have produced more than 180 million barrels of oil and 750 billion cubic feet of natural gas.
real_qa.requete: Iron Horse Aleo Energy wells failure rate track record

real_qa.q: What price does the EIA forecast for oil through 2026 and what does this mean for the fund's margin of safety?
real_qa.r: The Energy Information Administration forecasts that through 2026, oil prices will stay at $88 per barrel on average due to Strait of Hormuz constraints. The fund acquires wells at $65 WTI (West Texas Intermediate) pricing, providing a significant $23 per barrel buffer, while the break-even price for most operators is only $40 per barrel.

real_qa.q: What are the top producing basins where Iron Horse Energy invests in oil and gas wells?
real_qa.r: Iron Horse Energy invests exclusively in five top producing basins: the Permian (West Texas), the Eagle Ford (South Texas), the Anadarko (North Texas and Oklahoma), the Neobrara (Wyoming, Colorado and Nebraska), and the Bakken (North Dakota and Montana). The fund diversifies across approximately 40 or more wells to avoid concentration risk.
real_qa.requete: Iron Horse Energy Permian Eagle Ford Bakken basins

guest.bio_context: Courtney Muller is a partner at Iron Horse Energy and Aleo Energy who has been actively investing in oil and gas for many years. She is launching her third fund through Aleo Energy, having previously closed Iron Horse Energy Fund 1 at $31 million in December 2025 and Fund 2 at $10 million in June 2026. She and her partners have invested in more than 1,200 wells over the last 18-19 years with a less than 1% failure rate, producing over 180 million barrels of oil.
